baseline.description: A perturbation changes expression by the sum of its genes' single-gene changes in training (additive model).

lineage.hypothesis: RIDGE on the baseline features plus the built-in sum of each target gene's single-gene training change.
Adding an interaction between target_control_mean and additive_response improves prediction by capturing that high-expressed targets yield stronger additive effects.
Drop mean_response from the best model (EXP_0020) to test whether it still earns its place.
Drop control_mean from the best model (EXP_0024) to test whether it still earns its place.
Perturbations targeting hub genes (high PPI degree) produce larger expression changes across the genome.
Performance can be improved by tuning the ridge penalty alpha. [sweep alpha_grid=0.001]
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.001 for the best model (EXP_0085).
A random projection of the current best features plus a few weakly helpful features improves robustness and performance.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0108).
The optimal ridge penalty for the current best feature set plus newly proposed features lies in a narrower range around alpha=300. [sweep alpha_grid=1000]
Removing the is_target feature from the current best feature set will not significantly reduce performance, because additive_response already captures target-specific effects.

The effect of additive_response on a gene g is modulated by the average out-degree of perturbation p's target genes in the prior network, capturing how strongly p's targets propagate regulatory influence.
Tuning alpha for the current best feature set can improve performance. [sweep alpha_grid=1000]
Squaring the prior network outdegree before interacting with additive_response captures nonlinear regulatory influence and improves prediction.
The optimal ridge alpha for the current best feature set is not 0.01; a narrow sweep around this value may improve performance. [sweep alpha_grid=0.005]
The squared additive_response feature captures saturation or amplification effects that are not linear in the additive baseline.
The squared additive_response captures nonlinear saturation or amplification of perturbation effects.
The response of gene g in a CRISPRi screen (sign-corrected for CRISPRa) provides a direct prior for its change under any perturbation.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0365).
The number of transcription factors that regulate both targets of a pair perturbation predicts the response synergy or redundancy.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0374).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=300 for the best model (EXP_0387).
The product of target mean expression variance and additive_response improves prediction by modulating the additive baseline according to target variability.
Adding the product of gene_screen_delta_e365 and additive_response improves prediction.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0459).
The product of the number of gene sets containing both gene g and at least one target of perturbation p with additive_response improves prediction.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0486).
The product of average PPI degree and average prior-network out-degree of the perturbation's target genes, interacted with additive_response, captures combined network influence.
For pair perturbations, the Jaccard similarity of gene sets containing each target gene captures functional overlap and improves prediction.
The number of directed paths of length 2 in the prior network from any target of p to gene g is predictive.
The product of shortest path length between pair targets in PPI network and additive_response adds predictive power.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0580).
The square of pair_target_ppi_distance_x_additive_e580 adds predictive power.
The mean correlation between control expression of gene g and its direct PPI neighbors, weighted by PPI confidence, helps predict delta.
The average control-expression correlation among direct PPI neighbors of a perturbation's targets captures the functional module coherence of the targets and improves delta prediction.
The absolute value of additive_response multiplied by target_mean captures magnitude-dependent scaling of target expression effects.
The fraction of gene sets containing gene g that also contain at least one target of p adds information beyond the raw overlap count.
The specificity of a perturbation's target genes (inverse of number of gene sets they belong to) modulates the additive response.
The squared sign-corrected CRISPRi screen delta of gene g modulates the additive response, capturing non-linear dependence on the gene's intrinsic perturbation sensitivity.

most_useful_features.description: Concatenate several base features, standardize, then apply a fixed random Gaussian projection to reduce dimensionality.
Product of mean control expression of p's targets and the additive response row.
Average PPI network degree of the perturbation's target gene(s), broadcast to all genes.
Product of average PPI degree and average prior-network out-degree of the perturbation's target genes, multiplied by additive_response.
Random-walk-with-restart stationary probability over the PPI network, seeded uniformly on the target gene(s) of each perturbation.
Average PPI-network degree over the perturbation's target genes.
Squared average prior-network out-degree of p's target gene(s), multiplied row-wise by the additive response.
Shortest path length between pair targets in PPI network times additive_response; 0 for singles.
Heat kernel diffusion score from perturbation targets over the PPI network.
Product of additive_response and the percentile rank of the perturbation target's mean control expression (averaged for pairs).
